summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga (1901–1983) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki (~1923–1926), later serving as a professor at Kyoto University (~1950–1965).
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1990) and later as a professor (attested 2014).

August Fick (1833–1916) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1852–1856), later holding posts at Göttingen (~1869–1887) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Friedrich Pott (1802–1887) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen (~1821–1827) and Berlin (~1830–1833). He founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft and served as professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

August Johan Bernet Kempers (1906–1992) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Leiden University (~1924–1933), he directed the Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional (~1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien (1840–1916) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Kiel, Leipzig under Georg Curtius, and Jena under August Schleicher. He held posts at Göttingen and Jena before serving as professor at Leipzig University (~1870–1916).

August Schleicher (1821–1868) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Fleischer, Ewald, Ritschl, and Lassen. He completed his habilitation at Bonn (1846) and held posts at Charles University and Jena.

August Wilhelm Schlegel (1767–1845) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, founded Indische Bibliothek, and held professorial posts at Jena (~1796–1801) and Bonn (1818).

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as director of Aliah University (~1881–1899) and as secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.

Awadh Kishore Narain (1925–2013) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS, later holding posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1954–1971) and as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–1990).

Axel Michaels (born 1949) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1992–1996) and Heidelberg University (~1996–2018).

B. Alan Wallace (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under several traditional teachers, attended multiple institutions, and earned a PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt. He held posts at UCSB and the Santa Barbara Institute.

B. N. Mukherjee (1932–2013) was an Indian historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He completed his studies at the University of Calcutta (~1951–1954) and later held an academic post there (~1975–1997).

B. R. Ambedkar (1891–1956) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Elphinstone College, Columbia, LSE, Bonn, and the University of London, and served as professor of economics at Sydenham College (~1918–1920).

Baatr U. Kitinov works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. in World History at Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of the Department of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (1908–1994) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953), Joint/Deputy Director General at the ASI (~1953–1965), and Professor of Ancient Indian Culture and Archaeology at Panjab University (~1965–1973).
Baiei Henmi (1891–1977) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918) and later held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu (1919–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1945–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1952–1956), and as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and Institute of Philosophy (~1978–1995).

Baij Nath Puri (1916–1996) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1950–1952) and served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1957–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He completed his education at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1873–1877), Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai (~1877–1879).
